# Register reference {#registers}

This appendix lists the registers of LiteICLink: the controls of each SerDes wrapper,
the DRP access block, and the SerWB PHYs and core. It is generated from the register
definitions of the gateware, elaborated without running an FPGA toolchain. Every
configuration below is a design of the manual only (`doc/manual/registers.py`),
elaborated for this appendix on a LiteX-Boards platform: its clocks and pads are
placeholders and it is not a design to build. Offsets are in bytes from the base of
the bank; the base addresses depend on the SoC and are in the `csr.csv` of a build.
A build names a bank after the module of the SoC, `serdes0` for the SerDes wrapper of
the benches and `serwb_master_phy` for a SerWB PHY; this appendix names each one after
its family (`serdes_gtx`, `serwb_phy_s7`) to keep them apart. The Efinix SerWB PHY,
the Virtex-7 GTH and the UltraScale+ GTH are not elaborated: the notes describe their
banks by difference. The configurations, as the docstrings of `registers.py` describe
them:

- `gtp`: Artix-7 GTP on the quad PLL, reference clock from the fabric, clock aligner on
  (SQRL Acorn platform).
- `gtx_serwb`: Kintex-7 GTX on the CPLL with DRP access, and a 7-Series SerWB link master
  with every register option and a core with `with_crc=True` (KC705 platform).
- `gth3`: UltraScale GTH on the CPLL (KCU105 platform).
- `gty`: UltraScale+ GTY on the quad PLL, 40-bit words (XCU1525 platform).
- `ecp5`: ECP5 DCU 1, channel 0, at 2.5 Gbps (ECPIX-5 platform).
- `gtr12`: GW5AST-138 GTR12 lane with the status and UPAR registers, on a placeholder
  quad configuration (Tang Mega 138K Pro platform).
- `serwb_gen`: generic SerWB PHY as link master with every register option (iCEBreaker
  platform).

| Configuration | Target and options |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `gtp` | `doc/manual/registers.py` `soc_gtp` |
| `gtx_serwb` | `doc/manual/registers.py` `soc_gtx_serwb` |
| `gth3` | `doc/manual/registers.py` `soc_gth3` |
| `gty` | `doc/manual/registers.py` `soc_gty` |
| `ecp5` | `doc/manual/registers.py` `soc_ecp5` |
| `gtr12` | `doc/manual/registers.py` `soc_gtr12` |
| `serwb_gen` | `doc/manual/registers.py` `soc_serwb_gen` |

Access is `rw` for a register written by software (`CSRStorage`, or a `CSRStatus` that
software also writes, such as event pending bits cleared by writing 1), `ro` for a status
(`CSRStatus`) and `wo` for a write-only strobe (`CSR`). The reset value of a `CSRStorage`
register ends its description. A register wider than 32 bits takes several
32-bit words of the bus, most significant word first. The host scripts of `bench/` use these
names through the `csr.csv` of a build.

## GTP (Artix-7) {#reg-serdes-gtp}

Defined by `GTP` (`liteiclink/serdes/gtp_7series.py`).

The registers of `add_controls()` and `add_clock_cycles()`, the same on every Xilinx
wrapper except the electrical controls (see the notes of the other banks).
`clock_aligner_disable` exists only with `clock_aligner=True`, the default; the bench
targets build without the clock aligner. `clock_tx_cycles` and `clock_rx_cycles` are
written by the hardware when software writes `clock_latch`: read them, never write them.
Bit 2 of `rx_prbs_config` (`pause`) freezes `rx_prbs_errors` for a coherent read.

Bank `serdes_gtp`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `clock_aligner_` `disable` | `0x0000` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: Clock aligner enabled. `0b1`: Clock aligner disabled. Reset `0x0`. |
| `tx_enable` | `0x0004` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: TX disabled. `0b1`: TX enabled. Reset `0x1`. |
| `tx_ready` | `0x0008` | 1 | ro | `0b0`: TX not initialized. `0b1`: TX initialized and ready. |
| `tx_inhibit` | `0x000c` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: Normal operation. `0b1`: TX inhibited. Reset `0x0`. |
| `tx_produce_` `square_wave` | `0x0010` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: Normal operation. `0b1`: TX square wave generation enabled (linerate observation/checks). Reset `0x0`. |
| `rx_enable` | `0x0014` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: RX disabled. `0b1`: RX enabled. Reset `0x1`. |
| `rx_ready` | `0x0018` | 1 | ro | `0b0`: RX not initialized. `0b1`: RX initialized and ready. |
| `tx_prbs_config` | `0x001c` | 2 | rw | `0b00`: PRBS Disabled. `0b01`: PRBS7 Enabled. `0b10`: PRBS15 Enabled. `0b11`: PRBS31 Enabled. Reset `0x0`. |
| `rx_prbs_config` | `0x0020` | 3 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `rx_prbs_errors` | `0x0024` | 32 | ro | RX PRBS errors. |
| `loopback` | `0x0028` | 3 | rw | `0b000`: Normal operation. `0b001`: Near-End PCS Loopback. `0b010`: Near-End PMA Loopback. `0b100`: Far-End PMA Loopback. `0b110`: Far-End PCS Loopback. Reset `0x0`. |
| `tx_polarity` | `0x002c` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: Normal operation. `0b1`: TX polarity swap (equivalent to P/N swap). Reset `0x0`. |
| `rx_polarity` | `0x0030` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: Normal operation. `0b1`: RX polarity swap (equivalent to P/N swap). Reset `0x0`. |
| `tx_diffctrl` | `0x0034` | 4 | rw | TX Driver Swing Control, see UG482. Reset `0x8`. |
| `tx_postcursor` | `0x0038` | 5 | rw | TX Post Cursor Pre-emphasis Control, see UG482. Reset `0x0`. |
| `tx_postcursor_` `inv` | `0x003c` | 1 | rw | TX Post Cursor Polarity, see UG482. Reset `0x0`. |
| `tx_precursor` | `0x0040` | 5 | rw | TX Pre Cursor Pre-emphasis Control, see UG482. Reset `0x0`. |
| `tx_precursor_` `inv` | `0x0044` | 1 | rw | Invert polarity of TX Pre Cursor, see UG482. Reset `0x0`. |
| `clock_latch` | `0x0048` | 1 | rw | Write to latch TX/RX clock cycles. Reset `0x0`. |
| `clock_tx_cycles` | `0x004c` | 32 | ro | TX clock cycles. |
| `clock_rx_cycles` | `0x0050` | 32 | ro | RX clock cycles. |

Fields of `rx_prbs_config`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `config` | 1:0 | `0b00`: PRBS Disabled. `0b01`: PRBS7 Enabled. `0b10`: PRBS15 Enabled. `0b11`: PRBS31 Enabled. |
| `pause` | 2 | Pause RX PRBS. |

## DRP access {#reg-serdes-drp}

Defined by `DRPControl` (`liteiclink/serdes/common.py`).

Added by the design, not by the wrappers: `DRPControl(serdes.drp)` gives software access
to the dynamic reconfiguration port of a Xilinx channel. Software writes `addr`, `di`
and `we`, then any value to `start`, and polls `done` before reading `do`.

Bank `serdes_drp`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `addr` | `0x0000` | 9 | rw | DRP Address (9 bits). Reset `0x0`. |
| `di` | `0x0004` | 16 | rw | DRP Data In (16 bits) for write operation. Reset `0x0`. |
| `do` | `0x0008` | 16 | ro | DRP Data Out (16 bits) for read operation. |
| `we` | `0x000c` | 1 | rw | DRP Write Enable. Reset `0x0`. |
| `start` | `0x0010` | 1 | rw | Write to initiate DRP operation. Reset `0x0`. |
| `done` | `0x0014` | 1 | ro | DRP operation is complete. |

## ECP5 DCU {#reg-serdes-ecp5}

Defined by `SerDesECP5` (`liteiclink/serdes/serdes_ecp5.py`).

The base, PRBS and clock-cycle registers have the layout of the Xilinx banks, without
polarity and electrical controls; `loopback` takes the 3-bit modes of the Xilinx banks,
mapped to the DCU loopbacks, and `tx_inhibit` puts the TX output in electrical idle
([Lattice ECP5 DCU](#ecp5-controls)). The `sci_reconfig_` registers
are always present: they give software byte access to the SCI configuration registers
of the DCU (`sel` 0 for the channel, 1 for the dual), and `pause` stops the hardware
reconfiguration sequence while software uses them.

Bank `serdes_ecp5`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `sci_reconfig_` `pause` | `0x0000` | 1 | rw | Pause Hardware re-configuration. Reset `0x0`. |
| `sci_reconfig_` `sel` | `0x0004` | 1 | rw | Channel/Dual selection: 0 Channel / 1 Dual. Reset `0x0`. |
| `sci_reconfig_we` | `0x0008` | 1 | rw | Do a Write access. Reset `0x0`. |
| `sci_reconfig_re` | `0x000c` | 1 | rw | Do a Read access. Reset `0x0`. |
| `sci_reconfig_` `done` | `0x0010` | 1 | ro | Access is Done. |
| `sci_reconfig_` `adr` | `0x0014` | 6 | rw | Access address. Reset `0x0`. |
| `sci_reconfig_` `dat_w` | `0x0018` | 8 | rw | Access Write data. Reset `0x0`. |
| `sci_reconfig_` `dat_r` | `0x001c` | 8 | ro | Access Read data. |
| `tx_enable` | `0x0020` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: TX disabled. `0b1`: TX enabled. Reset `0x1`. |
| `tx_ready` | `0x0024` | 1 | ro | `0b0`: TX not initialized. `0b1`: TX initialized and ready. |
| `tx_inhibit` | `0x0028` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: Normal operation. `0b1`: TX inhibited. Reset `0x0`. |
| `tx_produce_` `square_wave` | `0x002c` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: Normal operation. `0b1`: TX square wave generation enabled (linerate observation/checks). Reset `0x0`. |
| `rx_enable` | `0x0030` | 1 | rw | `0b0`: RX disabled. `0b1`: RX enabled. Reset `0x1`. |
| `rx_ready` | `0x0034` | 1 | ro | `0b0`: RX not initialized. `0b1`: RX initialized and ready. |
| `tx_prbs_config` | `0x0038` | 2 | rw | `0b00`: PRBS Disabled. `0b01`: PRBS7 Enabled. `0b10`: PRBS15 Enabled. `0b11`: PRBS31 Enabled. Reset `0x0`. |
| `rx_prbs_config` | `0x003c` | 3 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `rx_prbs_errors` | `0x0040` | 32 | ro | RX PRBS errors. |
| `loopback` | `0x0044` | 3 | rw | Loopback: 0b000: Disabled / 0b001, 0b010: Near-End serial (TX to RX) / 0b100: Far-End serial (RX to TX) / 0b110: Far-End parallel (RX to TX). Reset `0x0`. |
| `clock_latch` | `0x0048` | 1 | rw | Write to latch TX/RX clock cycles. Reset `0x0`. |
| `clock_tx_cycles` | `0x004c` | 32 | ro | TX clock cycles. |
| `clock_rx_cycles` | `0x0050` | 32 | ro | RX clock cycles. |

## GTR12 (Gowin GW5) {#reg-serdes-gtr12}

Defined by `GTR12` (`liteiclink/serdes/gtr12_gw5.py`).

The GTR12 wrapper has no `add_controls()`: `add_status_csr()` adds `status` and
`upar.add_csr()` the `upar_` registers. The `upar_` registers reach the quad registers
at run time; requests of the user logic have priority over them
([Gowin GW5 GTR12](#gowin-gw5)).

Bank `serdes_gtr12`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `status` | `0x0000` | 29 | ro | pll_lock[0], cdr_lock[1], aligned[2], k_lock[3], rx_elecidle[4], astat[10:5], stat[23:11], refclk_det[25:24], plls_lock[28:26] (QPLL0, QPLL1, CPLL). |
| `upar_addr` | `0x0004` | 24 | rw | Register address. Reset `0x0`. |
| `upar_wrdata` | `0x0008` | 32 | rw | Register write data. Reset `0x0`. |
| `upar_ctrl` | `0x000c` | 2 | wo | Write strobe: bit 0 requests a write of `upar_wrdata` at `upar_addr`, bit 1 a read. |
| `upar_status` | `0x0010` | 3 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `upar_cfg` | `0x0014` | 1 | rw | Abort the access in progress (FSM back to idle). Reset `0x0`. |
| `upar_rddata` | `0x0018` | 32 | ro | Register read data. |

Fields of `upar_status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `ready` | 0 | No CSR access pending/in progress. |
| `upar_ready` | 1 | UPAR_READY_S. |
| `upar_rdvld` | 2 | UPAR_RDVLD_S. |

## SerWB PHY, 7-Series {#reg-serwb-phy-s7}

Defined by `SerdesControl` (`liteiclink/serwb/common.py`).

The `control_` registers of a high-speed SerWB PHY, here a 7-Series link master built
with `with_prbs=True` and `with_auto_retrain=True`. The UltraScale and Efinix PHYs have
the same bank; `control_phase` is meaningful on Efinix only. A link slave has no
`control_reset`: the master resets it through the link. `control_prbs_tx` and
`control_prbs_rx` exist only with `with_prbs=True`; without them, a link test counts the
received idle words that are not zero, which measures the link only without flow control
(with flow control the fill words are removed before the counter). `control_prbs_cycles`
counts `sys` cycles, and `control_prbs_errors` the words with one or more wrong bits.
`control_invalid_errors` counts the words with a symbol of an invalid ones count; it is cleared while the link
is not ready; it and `control_link_drops` stop at their maximum value.

Bank `serwb_phy_s7`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `control_reset` | `0x0000` | 1 | wo | Write strobe (link master only): restart the link initialization of both sides. |
| `control_ready` | `0x0004` | 1 | ro | 1: link initialized, words are exchanged. |
| `control_error` | `0x0008` | 1 | ro | 1: the initialization failed: no sampling window or word alignment found. |
| `control_delay` | `0x000c` | 9 | ro | Input delay (taps) chosen at the centre of the sampling window. |
| `control_delay_` `min_found` | `0x0010` | 1 | ro | 1: the lower edge of the sampling window was found. |
| `control_delay_` `min` | `0x0014` | 9 | ro | Lower edge of the sampling window (taps). |
| `control_delay_` `max_found` | `0x0018` | 1 | ro | 1: the upper edge of the sampling window was found. |
| `control_delay_` `max` | `0x001c` | 9 | ro | Upper edge of the sampling window (taps). |
| `control_shift` | `0x0020` | 6 | ro | Word alignment found by the initialization (bitslip). |
| `control_prbs_` `start` | `0x0024` | 1 | wo | Write strobe: clear `control_prbs_errors` and count errors for `control_prbs_cycles` cycles. |
| `control_prbs_` `cycles` | `0x0028` | 32 | rw | Duration of a link test, in `sys` cycles. Reset `0x0`. |
| `control_prbs_` `errors` | `0x002c` | 32 | ro | Errors counted by the last link test. |
| `control_` `invalid_errors` | `0x0030` | 32 | ro | Number of invalid 8b10b words received (link ready). |
| `control_link_` `drops` | `0x0034` | 32 | ro | Number of link losses (ready to not ready). |
| `control_prbs_tx` | `0x0038` | 1 | rw | Transmit PRBS31 instead of traffic (link ready). Reset `0x0`. |
| `control_prbs_rx` | `0x003c` | 1 | rw | Check received words against PRBS31 (traffic not forwarded). Reset `0x0`. |

## SerWB PHY, generic {#reg-serwb-phy-gen}

Defined by `SerdesControl` (`liteiclink/serwb/common.py`).

The generic PHY has no input delay: no `control_delay_` and no `control_phase`
registers. The other registers are those of the high-speed PHYs.

Bank `serwb_phy_gen`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `control_reset` | `0x0000` | 1 | wo | Write strobe (link master only): restart the link initialization of both sides. |
| `control_ready` | `0x0004` | 1 | ro | 1: link initialized, words are exchanged. |
| `control_error` | `0x0008` | 1 | ro | 1: the initialization failed: no sampling window or word alignment found. |
| `control_shift` | `0x000c` | 6 | ro | Word alignment found by the initialization (bitslip). |
| `control_prbs_` `start` | `0x0010` | 1 | wo | Write strobe: clear `control_prbs_errors` and count errors for `control_prbs_cycles` cycles. |
| `control_prbs_` `cycles` | `0x0014` | 32 | rw | Duration of a link test, in `sys` cycles. Reset `0x0`. |
| `control_prbs_` `errors` | `0x0018` | 32 | ro | Errors counted by the last link test. |
| `control_` `invalid_errors` | `0x001c` | 32 | ro | Number of invalid 8b10b words received (link ready). |
| `control_link_` `drops` | `0x0020` | 32 | ro | Number of link losses (ready to not ready). |
| `control_prbs_tx` | `0x0024` | 1 | rw | Transmit PRBS31 instead of traffic (link ready). Reset `0x0`. |
| `control_prbs_rx` | `0x0028` | 1 | rw | Check received words against PRBS31 (traffic not forwarded). Reset `0x0`. |

## SerWB core {#reg-serwb-core}

Defined by `SERWBCore` (`liteiclink/serwb/core.py`).

`crc_errors` exists only with `with_crc=True`, the option enabled here.
`rx_overflows` counts the events where a received packet word was lost because the RX
buffer of the core was full, which flow control avoids; lost idle words are not counted
([SerWB architecture](#serwb-architecture)).

Bank `serwb_core`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `crc_errors` | `0x0000` | 32 | ro | Number of packets dropped on CRC error. |
| `rx_overflows` | `0x0004` | 32 | ro | Number of RX overflows (received words lost). |
